Let $X\sim \mathbb{U}([0,1]), Y\sim \mathbb{U}([0,1]), X \perp Y$, what is $\mathbb{P}(1 \le X/Y \le2)$ ?



::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 💡 Hint

Compute the partial area corresponding to the meeting.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 💡 Solution

Since the two uniforms are positive, the possible region is $$\begin{cases} 0 \le x \le 1 \\ 0\le y \le 1\end{cases}.$$

The condition if fulfilled if  
$$\begin{cases} x / y\le 2\\  x/y \ge 1  \end{cases} \sim \begin{cases} y \le x \\  y \le x/2  \end{cases}.$$

We can plot the regions and we find $\boxed{\mathbb{P}(1 \le X/Y \le2) = \frac{1-\frac{1*1}{2}-\frac{1*1/2}{2}}{1}= 1/4.}$

```{python}
#| echo: false

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

n = 1000
x = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
y = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
X, Y = np.meshgrid(x, y)

possible = (X >= 0) & (Y >= 0) & (X <= 1) & (Y <= 1)

meeting = (
    possible &
    (Y <= X) &
    (Y >= X/2) )

plt.figure(figsize=(6,6))
plt.contourf(X, Y, possible, levels=[0.5,1], colors=["red"], alpha=0.5)
plt.contourf(X, Y, meeting, levels=[0.5,1], colors=["blue"], alpha=0.8)

plt.xlabel("x")
plt.ylabel("y")
plt.title("Ratio Region for uniform x, y")
plt.xlim(0,1)
plt.ylim(0,1)
plt.gca().set_aspect('equal')
plt.show()
```
:::


::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🚨 Generalisation

What if we wanted a ratio between p and q ?

Thus, $$\boxed{\mathbb{P}(p \le X/Y \le q) = 1-\frac{1*p}{2} -\frac{1*1/q}{2} = 1-\frac{p+1/q}{2}.}$$
:::
